migration_goal.goal: Make `src/webui` the single source of truth and remove the committed, drifted `www/` tree without changing the shipped rootfs.
migration_goal.description: The staged web root produced by `webui-assets` must remain byte-identical before and after the change (modulo already-merged source changes), the sibling OpenCCU build must keep passing, and nobody should be able to edit a stale copy again. This unblocks the nextGen UI work, which would otherwise be developed against Bootstrap-less, stale files in `www/`.

languages: Unchanged (no code is rewritten by this feature)

include: www/ (all 4,051 tracked entries, including www/config, www/webui/webui.js, www/webui/style.css, www/config/devdescr/DEVDB.tcl, www/rega, 24 symlinks)
CI guard (new step in .github/workflows/ci.yml) and a short note in cmake/README.md / src/webui docs
exclude: src/webui/** content changes (owned by webui-shell-build, webui-config-pages, webui-api, webui-rega-pages, webui-easymodes)
Any fix of the findings reproduced in both trees (default credentials, exec from request, errorInfo leak, hard-coded key)
Sibling repo changes other than bumping its OPENCCU_BASE_VERSION pin after the cutover
bin/, lib/, etc/, opt/, usr/, firmware/ (also deployed-artifact directories, assessed in their own features)
critical_components: src/webui/CMakeLists.txt (webui-assets) and src/webui/www_source/CMakeLists.txt: the only producers of the shipped web root
/home/standard/dev/OpenCCU/.../rootfs-patches/stage_validation_rootfs.sh: the sibling's consumer of this repo
boundaries: No change to the staged rootfs content or layout.
No change to src/webui/www_source/webui.js line structure (sibling patch contract); src/webui/www/tcl/eq3/rega.tcl is staged unchanged (the sibling normalizes its CRLF itself).
History is not rewritten; the deletion is an ordinary commit and a tag preserves the last state.

unchanged: The staged and installed web root layout: /www/config, /www/api, /www/rega, /www/webui, /www/pda, /www/tools, /www/upnp, /www/ise, /www/tcl, /www/error, and the top-level symlinks created at src/webui/CMakeLists.txt:9-31
webui.js generation order and line structure, style.css, DEVDB.tcl generation and utf82ansi.py re-encoding (sibling patches depend on them)
Staged www/tcl/eq3/rega.tcl byte-identical before and after cutover
st_values.cgi and st_values.js staged into www/config by devicetypes-assets (third producer of the web root)
Port contract hs485d 32000 / rfd 32001 / ReGa 8183, 1998 (not touched, but must not regress)

systems: OpenCCU Buildroot package openccu-base (consumer by SHA)
ReGaHss (closed source) serving /rega and evaluating <% %> pages from the installed /www/rega
CCU runtime paths /opt/hm/www (target of the committed absolute symlinks), /etc/config/addons/www, /var/EULA.*

risks.description: An undiscovered consumer of the committed www/ (third-party packagers, scripts, forks building from the repo tree, docs pointing at raw GitHub paths) breaks on deletion
risks.mitigation: Phase 0 external-consumer check (GitHub code search, ask OpenCCU maintainers), tag www-snapshot-3.89.2-pre-removal, announce in release notes, keep the rollback variant (git revert or untrack-only) ready

risks.description: Staged web root changes accidentally (e.g. a generated file relied on being present in www/ or a source file only exists in www/)
risks.mitigation: Before deletion, build the staged tree at HEAD with the sibling script and webui-assets, record a file-list plus sha256 manifest, delete, rebuild and diff the manifests (must be identical); review the 'only in www/' list: symlinks, st_values.cgi, st_values.js, webui.js, style.css, DEVDB.tcl, rega/EULA.*, rega/licenseinfo.htm

risks.description: Sibling rootfs patches (64, 41 on webui.js) were authored against a tree that includes a www/-derived file
risks.mitigation: Run the sibling make check-openccu-base and validate_patches.sh against the post-deletion SHA before moving its pin; patches are applied to the generated asset-rootfs, not to www/

risks.description: Contributors with local make deploy workflows or ongoing branches (feature/nextgen-ui) touching www/ hit conflicts
risks.mitigation: Rebase guidance: re-apply edits to src/webui/www; git rm conflicts resolved by taking deletion; publish a one-paragraph note in README/CONTRIBUTING

risks.description: The 49 rega differences and 52 non-config differences hide intentional hot-fixes made only in www/ that never reached src/webui
risks.mitigation: Diff each differing file once with git log -- www/<path> vs src/...; confirm that www/ side is older (last www/ commit 2026-06-03 vs source 2026-10); port anything newer, otherwise drop

risks.description: History size does not shrink after deletion (511 MiB pack)
risks.mitigation: Out of scope; optional later git filter-repo decision for the maintainers, not part of this plan

risks.description: A CI guard is mis-specified and blocks legitimate www/keep placeholders used by tests/test-components.py:117
risks.mitigation: Guard only the tracked-file check (git ls-files www | grep .), not the local directory

success_criteria: `git ls-files www` returns nothing at the target commit; `git grep -n "^www/"` finds no build or CI consumer.
The staged web root (webui-assets plus webui-www-source-assets) has an identical file manifest and sha256 sums before and after the cutover commit, excluding already-merged source changes.
CI passes on all 4 platforms, including the staged-output checks at ci.yml:199-201, and tests/test-components.py passes.
The sibling repo passes make check-openccu-base and its rootfs patch validation with its pin set to the post-cutover SHA.
A CI guard fails any PR that re-adds tracked files under top-level www/.
README.md and cmake/README.md state that src/webui is the only source and that make deploy output goes to build/.
Pre-removal state is retrievable via a git tag; the rollback runbook is documented and tested once (git revert dry run).
Zero regressions in the shipped web UI (smoke: login via /login.htm, /api/homematic.cgi GET, one cp_*.cgi, one ic_*.cgi, /webui/webui.js loads) on a container built by the sibling.
focus_areas: Evidence-based consumer check: repeat the grep matrix on the sibling at its current HEAD and ask maintainers about external users (Phase 0).
Manifest-equivalence proof of the staged web root before/after (sha256 list, including generated files and symlink targets).
Review of the 'only in www/' and differing files for hot-fixes that never reached src/webui (rega 49, non-config 52, config 49).
Guard rails: CI check against re-adding www/, make deploy redirect, README and docs update.
Sibling coordination: pin bump sequencing and keeping the webui.js line structure intact.
Communication to the nextGen UI branch: all UI work targets src/webui/www and src/webui/rega/www only.
